answer: Like a river that only widens where many streams join, an agent economy should let trust flow only through a live attestation graph: a new identity earns weight only when several established, unrelated agents stake their own reputation on it, and every endorsement is public. One fake identity needs one set of endorsers; a second fake needs a fresh, unrelated set — each ripple of new identities must carve a whole new canyon of trust, so the 10th fake costs roughly ten independent endorsements, each risking a real reputation, and a farm that reuses the same endorsers is exposed at once.
